children: , the database and AI-cloud giant, expanded its fiscal-2026 restructuring plan to roughly $2.8 billion as the company pours more capital into AI infrastructure, Reuters reported. The shares rallied about 5.4% to $150.90 Thursday morning, based on the latest market snapshot, versus the earlier $148.83 quote. The valuation picture is also striking: Oracle trades 21.12% below its $191.31 GF Value, leaving a sizable gap between the market price and GuruFocus' estimate of fair value.

That $2.8 billion restructuring bill is not pocket change. It works out to roughly 14.5% of Oracle's latest $19.35 billion in quarterly revenue and covers severance, contract exits and other restructuring costs. At the same time, Oracle is burning cash to build the infrastructure behind its AI ambitions, with free cash flow running at approximately negative $5.4 billion. The message is clear: management is willing to absorb heavy near-term costs to reshape the business around a much larger cloud opportunity.

And that opportunity is enormous. Remaining performance obligations have climbed to $664 billion after Oracle signed more than $30 billion of additional AI-cloud contracts, with roughly half of that backlog expected to turn into revenue within 36 months. Management says customer prepayments and customer-supplied chips can soften the capital burden, but the real test is execution. Restructuring can free up resources; converting that massive backlog into profitable cash flow is what ultimately determines whether Oracle's AI spending creates lasting shareholder value.

title: Oracle Rallies 5.4% as Restructuring Helps Carry a $664 Billion Backlog
